gaps.title: Fix the voting machines — then the money was cut to zero
gaps.law: Help America Vote Act of 2002 (Pub. L. 107-252)
gaps.authorized: ~$3.86B total; incl. 'requirements payments' to help states meet federal voting-system standards
gaps.appropriated: Requirements payments eliminated to $0 in FY2005–FY2007; ~$672–727M of authorized requirements funds left unappropriated
gaps.constituent: County election offices modernizing registration & accessible voting systems
gaps.note: HAVA ultimately disbursed billions over time; the documented gap is the FY05–07 window when requirements funding was zeroed. Advocate/legislator figures ($672M vs $727M) vary by date.

gaps.title: Civil-rights cold cases: the funding never came
gaps.law: Emmett Till Unsolved Civil Rights Crime Act of 2007
gaps.authorized: ~$13.5M/yr (FY2008–2017; reauthorized 2016): $10M to DOJ/FBI for federal cold-case work, $2M for state/local grants, $1.5M to the Community Relations Service
gaps.appropriated: $0 — per the Attorney General's First Annual Report (2009): 'funds authorized by this Act have not been appropriated'; DOJ met its duties by diverting existing resources
gaps.constituent: Families seeking justice in unsolved civil-rights-era killings
gaps.note: Authoritative DOJ primary source. A SEPARATE OJP/BJA grant program (created by the 2016 reauthorization) later provided ~$2–3M/yr to state/local agencies — still a fraction of the authorization, and the $10M DOJ/FBI stream was never appropriated as a dedicated line. (Earlier draft wrongly measured the $10M authorization against those later grants.)

gaps.title: A national ID standard, funded at two cents on the dollar
gaps.law: REAL ID Act of 2005 (Pub. L. 109-13, Div. B)
gaps.authorized: National driver's-license/ID standards; DHS estimated ~$3.9B cost to states (~$9.9B total nationwide)
gaps.appropriated: ≈ $90M in federal grants (e.g., $40M in 2005 + $50M FY2008 omnibus)
gaps.gapLabel: ~$3.8B of the estimated state burden left to the states
gaps.constituent: State DMVs and the residents who fund them
gaps.note: Deliverable-based: the dollar figure is DHS's own cost estimate (final rule), not an authorized $ amount. Grants cited are early cumulative; critics put federal support at <1% of estimated cost.

gaps.title: The signature prison-reform law, zeroed out in year one
gaps.authorized: $75,000,000 per year, FY2019–FY2023, for recidivism-reduction programs (80% to the Bureau of Prisons)
gaps.appropriated: $0 formally appropriated in FY2019 (DOJ redirected ~$75M of existing funds as a stopgap); FY2020 request only ~$14M
gaps.gapLabel: The full $75M authorization went unappropriated in the first year
gaps.constituent: Incarcerated people eligible for earned-time programming, and the BOP
gaps.note: FY2019 requirements funding was $0; DOJ covered it by shifting internal money, and later appropriations provided partial funding. The year-one $0 is the documented gap.

gaps.title: An interstate system — on paper for twelve years
gaps.authorized: Designation of the 'National System of Interstate Highways'
gaps.appropriated: $0 for construction (1944–1952); a token $25M/yr arrived in 1952
gaps.gapLabel: The entire interstate network sat unfunded until the 1956 Highway Trust Fund
gaps.constituent: The traveling public — a nation with the plan but not the pavement
gaps.note: Resolved by the 1956 act. Included as the classic teaching anchor and proof that these gaps can be closed.

gaps.title: Special education's 'forty percent' promise
gaps.authorized: Federal commitment to fund 40% of the excess cost of special education
gaps.appropriated: ~13% of excess cost (FY2020) — the federal share has never reached half the commitment
gaps.constituent: Local school districts and property taxpayers
gaps.note: Target-shortfall (not ≤5%): the 40% is a commitment, not a hard appropriation cap. Peaked near ~33% once (2009 stimulus).
sources: House Ed & Workforce — IDEA Funding Gap

gaps.title: The conservation fund that collected, then sat
gaps.law: Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965
gaps.appropriated: Far less in most years (e.g., ~$495M FY2020); fully funded only ~twice in the program's history
gaps.constituent: State parks, trails, and public-lands projects
gaps.note: Resolved: the Great American Outdoors Act (2020) made the full $900M mandatory. Proof these gaps can close.

gaps.title: Rural counties, cut off from the promise
gaps.law: Secure Rural Schools and Community Self-Determination Act of 2000
gaps.authorized: Revenue-sharing payments to timber counties (in lieu of lost federal-land logging receipts)
gaps.appropriated: Reauthorization lapsed in 2023; fallback leaves counties with an average ~80% reduction
gaps.constituent: Rural schools and county roads in 41 states
gaps.note: Lifecycle: lapsed 2023. Status flips if/when Congress reauthorizes and backfills FY2024–25.
